links.outcome: Clinical composition of health LLM benchmarks versus real-world needs
links.effect: Benchmarks lack raw clinical artifacts: laboratory values 5.2%, imaging 3.8%, raw medical records 0.6%; chronic disease management only 5.5%; benchmark composition misaligned with real-world clinical needs.
links.quote: Evaluation benchmarks remain misaligned with real-world clinical needs, lacking raw clinical artifacts, adequate representation of vulnerable populations, and longitudinal chronic care scenarios.

links.outcome: Representation of safety-critical scenarios in benchmarks
links.effect: Suicide/self-harm queries comprised <0.7% of the corpus; safety-critical scenarios effectively absent.
links.quote: Safety-critical scenarios were effectively absent: suicide/self-harm queries comprised <0.7% of the corpus and chronic disease management only 5.5%.

links.outcome: Representation of vulnerable populations in benchmark queries
links.effect: Pediatrics and older adults each below 11% of the corpus; global health needs neglected.
links.quote: Benchmarks also neglected vulnerable populations (pediatrics/older adults <11%) and global health needs.

unlisted_practices: Standardized query profiling of benchmark composition analogous to clinical trial reporting

screen.reason: The study conducts an empirical cross-sectional audit of health AI benchmark query datasets, evaluating their composition, clinical validity, and representation of vulnerable/safety-critical populations.
